entries.architecture: eleven source kinds incl. remote folder over SFTP
entries.comparison: remote folder source (SFTP, key-only auth, strict known_hosts, path allowlist, no shell); catalog order 1-11; IM plan changes to vendored transports without a dsh-im runtime dependency

entries.architecture: eleven source kinds; DingTalk stream transport
entries.comparison: DingTalk source receives direct and group @ messages over stream and replies through the session webhook or robot API; token cache, per-instance health and reconnect; public dingtalk-stream SDK with dsh-im protocol attribution, no dsh-im runtime dependency

entries.architecture: eleven source kinds; QQ bot gateway transport
entries.comparison: QQ source receives direct and group @ messages over the bot gateway and replies passively with a stable msg_seq; markdown fallback, gone on expired windows, per-instance health; public qqbot-nodejs SDK with dsh-im protocol attribution, no dsh-im runtime dependency

entries.architecture: eleven source kinds; WeChat iLink transport
entries.comparison: WeChat source logs in by QR over iLink, stores the bot token in local KV, receives whitelisted direct text messages and replies in the same conversation; group messages ignored for now; protocol adapted from dsh-im with attribution, no dsh-im runtime dependency

entries.architecture: eleven source kinds; DingTalk inbound attachments
entries.comparison: DingTalk source downloads inbound picture/file attachments into the state directory and hands their absolute paths to the worker through the Trigger; limits, trusted hosts and path sanitizing; outbound attachments still text-only

entries.architecture: eleven source kinds; DingTalk and QQ inbound attachments
entries.comparison: QQ source downloads inbound image/file attachments from trusted Tencent CDN hosts into the state directory with size/count limits and hands their paths to the worker; outbound attachments still text-only

entries.architecture: eleven source kinds; DingTalk, QQ and WeChat inbound attachments
entries.comparison: WeChat source downloads inbound image/file attachments from the trusted iLink CDN, decrypts them with AES-128-ECB and saves them under the state directory; all three IM channels now accept inbound attachments, while outbound attachments remain text-only and WeChat groups stay unsupported by iLink

entries.architecture: eleven source kinds; attachments both ways on DingTalk and inbound on WeChat/QQ
entries.comparison: DingTalk sends a ticket's deliverables back as file/image messages after the text reply, through the core OutboundMessage.attachments path; other channels ignore attachments for now

entries.architecture: twelve source kinds incl. web feed monitor
entries.comparison: Web page/feed Source (RSS/Atom/JSON, baseline, dedupe, SSRF guards) at order 3; DingTalk scan-to-create onboarding with server-side account creation; WeChat QR image fix; QQ scan tab marked under development while manual stays; bot creation links and steps

entries.architecture: twelve source kinds; QQ scan onboarding
entries.comparison: QQ scan-to-create onboarding reimplemented from the public bind protocol (create_bind_task, AES-256-GCM secret decrypt) without the UNLICENSED connector; server creates the QQ account and seeds the scanner openid into the allow-list; secret never returns to the browser

entries.architecture: twelve source kinds; secret-free settings history and unique account names
entries.comparison: Configuration history reports a credential only as set, replaced or cleared and never returns its value; an account's display name is editable in its settings form and kept unique across accounts (case-insensitively), with scan-created accounts taking numbered names
